deltas.delta: The v0.16.7 upgrade instructions state that they apply only to testnet and that deployment dates will be announced later. The release table still lists v0.16.7 for mainnet as N/A, and v0.16.5 (mainnet 2026-10-22) is the last mainnet release.

The release notes of v0.16.6 list PR #2667, which makes the compiler check memory bounds once per offset stack element. No earlier cycle named this PR. It is the touch_memory cache that cycle 13 read: the second access through the same non-literal offset element skips the check only when the first access, which always runs earlier in the same straight-line block, covered at least as many bytes (emitter.cpp lines 6300 to 6312 at v0.16.7). The cache is in v0.16.6 and v0.16.7 only, which validators do not run.

findings.title: MegaETH skips every later candidate of a block once one transaction fills the block budget for new state, and the specification leaves the order of reconsideration to the sequencer
findings.difference: MegaETH enforces block-level runtime limits on state growth, KV updates and data size. Once a block meets one of them, the node skips every later candidate before execution. The block-level state growth limit equals the per-transaction one (1,000 entries), so a single transaction can reach it. Ethereum has no such per-block limit.
findings.mechanism: The specification now states the rule in normative form. The first transaction that brings cumulative block usage to the limit is still included, and every later candidate of that block is skipped, gets no receipt and may be reconsidered in a later block. limit.rs, executor.rs, chain.rs and constants.rs on mega-evm main are byte identical to v1.7.4, so the rule and the 1,000 entry limits are unchanged. A filler transaction that writes 1,000 fresh slots in minimum-size buckets costs about 22.6 million gas, as cycle 19 computed. Any modifyLiquidity, take, burn or swap sent to the PoolManager after it in the same block is skipped and runs in a later block with the same checks and amounts. Its outcome does not change, since no PoolManager path reads block number, time or position in a block (src/PoolManager.sol:103-114, 291-297). The amplified form, in which N fillers close N blocks to every later arrival, needs skipped transactions to keep their place ahead of newer ones. The specification says only 'may be reconsidered', so that part rests on the closed sequencer's policy. No block of the 20,001 cycle 19 read came near the limit. This part of the finding is the same hazard as F-042. F-062 adds only the unconfirmed queue rule, and the two should be merged.
findings.impact: No funds move and no balance becomes unwithdrawable. Swaps, liquidity removals and claim burns of other users are delayed by one block per filler. A longer delay needs the queue rule, which no public source states.
findings.preconditions: The base fee stays near its floor, the sequencer does not filter the filling sender, and for the amplified form skipped transactions keep their place in the queue.
findings.mitigations: Exits under load can use an L1 deposit. The operator can set the block-level state growth limit above the per-transaction one, price state growth in minimum-size buckets, or deprioritise senders who reach the block budget.

sources.supports: Runtime block-level limits: later candidates are skipped once a block is at or above the limit, skipped transactions get no receipt and may be reconsidered in a later block, and the per-transaction gas cap is sequencer-configured

cleared.check: Monad PR #2667 (v0.16.6), which checks memory bounds once per offset stack element in compiled code. Can a compiled MLOAD or MSTORE skip an expansion it needs?
cleared.result: No. touch_memory serves only accesses of at most 32 bytes (MLOAD, MSTORE, MSTORE8) and skips the check only when the same immutable stack element has already been checked for at least as many bytes. That earlier check runs before it in the same straight-line block, or in a fall-through block that is not a jump destination (emitter.cpp jumpi, lines 3516 to 3536 on main). Memory never shrinks within a frame, and a failed check leaves the frame. The path exists only in v0.16.6 and later, which validators do not run, and simulated calls use the interpreter.

cleared.check: Monad MONAD_NINE memory cap (8 MB per transaction, counted over the current frame and its parents), measured on the live interpreter. Can an ordinary account use it to make a PoolManager call of another user fail, or to make the PoolManager continue after a failed sub-call?
cleared.result: The cap holds at its exact edge: a write ending at byte 8,388,608 succeeds and one ending at 8,388,640 fails as out of gas. Only frames of the same transaction count, so an outside account can reach a victim's PoolManager call only through a hook or token in the victim's pool (pool-creator). Every PoolManager sub-call treats failure as a revert of the whole call: hook calls at src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-135, payouts at src/types/Currency.sol:44-80, and the revert wrapper at src/libraries/CustomRevert.sol:84-112. No path continues past a frame that the cap stopped. A hook that returns several MB makes its own pool's calls fail through the copy at Hooks.sol:140-149, which is a pool-creator hazard already covered by F-004.
cleared.source: https://docs.monad.xyz/developer-essentials/opcode-pricing and eth_call on https://rpc.monad.xyz with initcode 0x6001627fffe05200 (result 0x) and 0x600162800000520000 (out of gas)

cleared.check: Lead L-933: can a transaction from Monad SYSTEM_SENDER, whose key system_sender.hpp calls known, reach the staking reward, snapshot or epoch change functions?
cleared.result: No such path was found. The three syscalls are dispatched only in ExecuteSystemTransaction::execute_staking_syscall (execute_system_transaction.cpp lines 209 to 233). The staking precompile's dispatch table has no REWARD, SNAPSHOT or ON_EPOCH_CHANGE case and falls back to precompile_fallback. A system transaction must be legacy, addressed to the staking contract, with gas limit and fee 0 (validate_system_transaction.cpp lines 41 to 75), which an ordinary transaction cannot pass because of its intrinsic gas. The system sender cannot appear in an authorization list (validate_monad_transaction.cpp line 53). eth_call from the system sender with REWARD and SNAPSHOT reverts with 'method not supported'. Whether the key itself is published was not found. The address is not the PoolManager or its owner.

leads.question: When Monad publishes a mainnet date for any release after v0.16.5, read the emitter diff of that tag against v0.16.5 for arithmetic, shift, comparison, JUMPI and memory handlers, and rebuild the cycle 16 harness on it if the asmjit API migration on main is part of it.
leads.why: Main moves the x86 emitter to a new asmjit API across 564 changed lines. A changed operand or register mapping in a multiply, shift or comparison would reach compiled blocks before any simulated call can see it, and FullMath.mulDiv and TickBitmap use those shapes on every swap.

leads.question: Does MegaETH's sequencer keep transactions skipped for a block budget ahead of later arrivals? A census of blocks after one that reached the state growth limit would show it, once such a block exists.
leads.why: This is the only open link of F-062. If skipped transactions keep their place, N fillers delay all later PoolManager exits by N blocks.

leadResults.answer: All 75 MegaETH blocks with a PoolManager log from 32,826,735 to head 32,842,064 validate in the public stateless validator with the pre-state tied to the parent hash. The battery (99,985) and targeted set (85,544) match on mega-reth/v2.3.1-4499c42, and pmdiff and pmdiff2 match 250 of 250 and 300 of 300.

Validators run v0.16.5 by the official schedule: the v0.16.7 upgrade instructions say they apply to testnet only, and the release table lists v0.16.7 for mainnet as N/A. The RPC answers Monad/0.16.7, and the battery, the targeted set, pmdiff and pmdiff2 match there, with the same 21 and 20 gas-bound scripts as in cycle 19. No tag after v0.16.7 exists (404 for v0.16.8, v0.16.9, v0.17.0, v0.17.1). On main the emitter, its header, uint256.hpp and math.hpp equal cycle 19's copies. The change from v0.16.7 to main is mostly the asmjit API migration, which is carried as a new lead for when a release ships it.

Nothing new is public. The resource limits specification describes only node behaviour and names no public method that the sequencer executes. mega-evm main still equals v1.7.4 and no new tag exists. Mined evidence grew by 75 anchored PoolManager blocks, all matching stock revm, which is still the only public check of the producer's compiled path.

The resource limits specification says the transaction gas limit must fit a 'sequencer-configured per-transaction gas cap' and gives no value. constants.rs fixes only compute gas caps (TX_COMPUTE_GAS_LIMIT 1,000,000,000 and 200,000,000 under different specs), not total gas. The configured value remains unpublished.

Two Upgraded events from block 0 to head: 0x31f6e6a3 (OptimismPortal2 3.14.0) at creation (block 23,770,457) and 0x55400445 (3.15.2) at block 24,036,326, made through ProxyAdmin.upgrade. No temporary implementation was ever set.

discard_tx was added in mega-evm v1.7.3 (pull request 405) and is absent from v1.7.2. It clears the journal, transient storage, the frame stack and the cached L1 cost after a caught panic. Whether the closed producer caught panics earlier, and which mega-evm the replica build pins, is not public. No known input panics revm 40.0.3 or mega-evm. The panic sites in execution.rs are internal invariants. A carried unlock flag or delta would change the result of a later PoolManager transaction in the same block, and the 75 anchored blocks of this cycle plus the earlier ones show no such change.

The replica build string is unchanged (mega-reth/v2.3.1-4499c42) and no mega-evm release followed v1.7.4. The validator was nonetheless rerun on every PoolManager block from 32,826,735 to 32,842,064 (75 blocks), all valid. Rerun when either string changes.

The staking syscalls are reachable only through the separate system transaction path, which requires sender SYSTEM_SENDER, a legacy type, the staking address and zero gas and fee. The precompile dispatch has no syscall selector, and eth_call from the system sender with REWARD and SNAPSHOT reverts with 'method not supported'. Whether the key is published was not found, and the address is not the PoolManager's.

No block or vote field names a version. The v0.16.7 upgrade instructions say they apply to testnet only, so mainnet validators are on v0.16.5 by the official schedule. Both releases give the same PoolManager results by the cycle 17 proof.
